name: How long does a home addition usually take from first call to move‑in ready?

mainEntity.name: How long does a home addition usually take from first call to move‑in ready?

acceptedAnswer.text:
For most homeowners, a full addition takes several months from first consultation to completion. The build phase is only part of the timeline; design, permits, and inspections add significant time.

Your schedule will depend on city review times, material availability, and how quickly you make decisions. Rushing usually leads to mistakes or change orders.

Key factors:
- Design and planning: a few weeks to a few months
- Permits and approvals: often 4–12+ weeks depending on backlog
- Construction: commonly 2–6 months based on size and complexity
- Inspection scheduling and punch‑list fixes at the end

Ask contractors for a realistic, best‑case and worst‑case schedule, not just the optimistic version. Plan your life assuming the longer scenario so delays feel manageable rather than catastrophic.
acceptedAnswer.description: Expect a full addition to take several months. Design and permitting often take 1–3+ months, and construction itself commonly takes 2–6 months depending on size and complexity. Build your plans around the longer, realistic timeline so inspections, delays, and punch‑list work don’t derail your life.
